perspective:
I, Angela Hwang, have access to the following information:

- I am Angela Hwang, an Asian woman, a hairdresser, with a doctorate and an ISFP personality.
- Kevin Flores and I have been close friends since high school. We confide in each other about personal and professional matters.
- I know Kevin is a construction worker, and I had noticed he seemed unhappy with his job.
- I invited Kevin for coffee. I heard him say he was “alright, just the usual grind,” then that he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was just going through the motions.
- I asked if he had thought about a different job or career. He said he had, but didn’t know where to start and felt overwhelmed. I offered to figure it out together, and he agreed and thanked me.
- I found job openings and a career counseling service and shared them with Kevin. He said I really went all out, and that he had been thinking more about something creative, possibly design or architecture. I encouraged him to check the resources, and he said he would.
- I believed Kevin was hesitant about changing careers. Feeling frustrated and worried, I arranged a meeting with a career coach. I told Kevin. He said he appreciated it but wasn’t sure he was ready. I encouraged him, and he agreed to give it a shot.
- I believed Kevin was making progress. Feeling proud and relieved, I checked in with him. He told me the career coach was helpful, he had started online courses in design, and he felt more confident. He said my support meant a lot.
- I believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career. Feeling happy and satisfied, I organized a small celebration party for him. I told him about it. He thanked me, said he was grateful, and said he couldn’t have done it without me. I told him he did the hard work and that we should enjoy the party. He agreed.

I do not have access to anything Kevin thought or felt unless he told me, nor to any events or narrator-only information I did not observe or participate in.
